payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_history_run.py::test_the_history_command_reads_a_writable_copy_and_never_writes_the_mount stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'The history mount declared without `readonly`.' applied to saffron/cell/session.py as an edit. The claim was "`session.run_history` enters a Gate-only cell through `critic_cell`, with `network=None`, the repo's `thread_env` alone as its env, and read-only bind mounts as its `extra_mounts`. One sits at `worktree.HISTORY_MOUNT`. Its source is `session.HISTORY_SOURCE_ROOT` joined with the spec id, a directory that holds the ledger's snapshot and is never the live ledger's directory, emptied before the snapshot is written. One sits at `worktree.MIRRORS_MOUNT`, and its source is `mirror.parent`, the directory holding the host's mirrors. With `batches: true` one more sits at `worktree.BATCHES_MOUNT`, and its source is `out_dir` itself, never a copy. With `batches` false there is no batch tree mount. Every mount is a `bind` with `readonly` set. Both execs in the cell go through `runtime.exec_`, from `worktree.WORKTREE_MOUNT`, with a timeout of 600 seconds. The command sees `SAFFRON_HISTORY_HOME` naming a home under `worktree.STATE_MOUNT`. That home holds a writable copy of the mount's `ledger.db`, with the batch tree linked read-only as `v0` under `batches` when it is mounted. In that copy, each repo's `mirror_path` names the same mirror under `worktree.MIRRORS_MOUNT`. So the projection, run as the command over a ledger whose `mirror_path` is a host path the cell cannot see, finds the spec in a real git mirror and leaves no task out as `spec_not_found`. A command that writes to its ledger leaves every file of every mount source unchanged. The result carries the exit code, stdout and stderr. The snapshot's directory is gone once `run_history` returns, and also after `critic_cell` raises. The witness drives `batches` true and false, a stale file left in the snapshot's directory, and a `critic_cell` that raises.", and only that witness ran under the edit.
